status: Design and capacity calculation; no new search or index build launched
reference: The same frozen comprehensive core_nt; no NR substitution or taxonomic subset

six_complete_frames.excluded_overheads: FASTA headers, original nucleotide payload, taxonomic/provenance maps, indexes and temporary storage

MMseqs2_index_capacity.interpretation: Capacity estimate for an unfiltered complete-frame representation, not a measured MMseqs2 build. The normal ORF-splitting representation has a different residue/sequence count; dropping short ORFs changes sensitivity. Splitting the index changes resident memory but does not establish wall-time or disk cost.

candidate_designs.name: Native tblastx word4
candidate_designs.evidence: Completed 43-mate pilot preserved all mate statuses and LCAs at both thresholds, with 4.63x lower elapsed time than default word size 3. Larger 464-mate run pending.
candidate_designs.costs_unmeasured: Production batching and full candidate-population cost.

candidate_designs.name: Consolidate native tblastx query batches
candidate_designs.mechanism: The inspected official implementation uses 10,002 nucleotide bases per translated-query batch and runs the reference search separately for every batch. BATCH_SIZE provides an explicit override. The frozen 464-mate input totals 67,905 bases and models seven batches.
candidate_designs.evidence: The running output prefix contains exactly the first 137 query mates, matching the first two modeled batches. This is a progress observation, not a completed timing comparison.
constraints: Inspected repository source is not asserted to be the exact source revision of the pinned executable.
Larger batches can increase lookup and extension work; speedup is unmeasured.
Raw alignment multiset and per-read taxonomic parity must be compared, not assumed.
Only consider a bounded replay of existing queries after the current panel completes; no larger biological panel or new reference.

candidate_designs.name: Materialize all six frames and use a protein index
candidate_designs.mechanism: Retain original nucleotide accession, strand, frame, coordinate and all taxonomic mappings. Translate all reference sequences, including nonviral sequences. Search each query independently; merge evidence by original subject before existing ranking.
constraints: Retain short and stop-containing sequence evidence rather than silently discarding it.
Protein score statistics and target/HSP limits need measured comparison to native tblastx.
Measured extraction/index-build time, peak memory, peak disk and output sizes required before a full build.
No full build launched; current workers lack space for a naive multi-terabyte intermediate plus index.

candidate_designs.name: MMseqs2 translated nucleotide search
candidate_designs.mechanism: Native translated search accepts nucleotide query and target inputs with search type 2. Default ORF extraction splits at stops and requires 30 amino acids.
constraints: Default minimum ORF length would exclude the known 21-amino-acid short-read example.
Lowering minimum length does not reproduce alignments spanning stop codons.
Target splitting, global result merging and report caps must preserve each read’s own competing taxa.
No executable installed or search launched for this candidate.

candidate_designs.name: Codon-aware spaced nucleotide seeding
candidate_designs.mechanism: dc-megablast coding templates tolerate third-position mismatches during seeding while retaining the existing nucleotide database.
constraints: This remains nucleotide scoring and is not equivalent to amino-acid homology.
Synonymous differences affecting the first or second codon bases are not all covered.
A bounded small-panel comparison could measure cost and discrepancies before considering it further.
No search launched; do not compete for CPU with either active measurement.

limits: No new biological conclusion follows from these resource calculations or documented tool options.
The existing selected diagnostic panels cannot establish accuracy or full-public-dataset detection gains.
Future comparisons must preserve the original observations and use a separate source commit per approach.
